name: Pumice-Wraith
specific_features: Automated beacon (distress, navigation, or unknown purpose)
description: Pumice-Wraith is a pale, porous world that looks like it was carved from volcanic pumice and set adrift. The surface is covered in fine, light-gray dust that fills ancient craters and flows like liquid in the low gravity, forming slow-moving dust seas that shift with the planet's rotation. The rock beneath is riddled with vesicles and voids, making the entire planet unnervingly light for its size.

The thin atmosphere scatters light unevenly, creating ghostly halos and false horizons that give the planet its spectral name. Walking the surface stirs up dust that hangs in the air for hours, reducing visibility to meters. Magnetic anomalies near the poles cause compasses to spin and navigation equipment to give contradictory readings, as though the planet's core has no consistent magnetic field.

An automated beacon has broadcast from Pumice-Wraith's largest crater for at least two centuries, predating any known survey of the system. The beacon transmits on a non-standard frequency in a format that resists decryption, and its power source has never been identified. The crater around it is conspicuously dust-free, as though something repels the ever-present particulate.

Salvage crews and signal analysts have both attempted to reach the beacon, but the magnetic anomalies make precision landing difficult, and surface navigation is unreliable. Those who have come close report their equipment behaving erratically, and one team claimed to see structured light patterns emanating from the beacon at close range. Pumice-Wraith offers little of material value, but the beacon ensures it is never entirely forgotten.
